# Plan for ISSUE-200

Keep mandatory guidance in every prompt while making optional guidance discoverable and selectively inline. Work is confined to bundle generation, regression coverage, and a changelog fragment.

## Shape

**Involved**: bundle composition, optional guidance selection, trusted references, and issue/PR compatibility require coordinated changes, but fit one implementation cycle.

## What we know

- `internal/workspace/worktree.go:774` loads role and repository guidance using `baseSHA`; lines 804–822 currently inline all Markdown rules and skills without selection.
- `internal/workspace/worktree.go:844` writes active files through `safefs`; lines 871–874 write WORKUNIT.md and lines 909–910 append that same text to SYSTEM_PROMPT.md.
- `internal/workspace/worktree.go:877` starts with the role prompt; validation policy and planner budget follow optional guidance. Planner review feedback is already near the end.
- `internal/workspace/pr.go:21` delegates PR bundle generation to CompileHarnessBundleAt, so shared changes cover both lifecycles.
- `.swarm/skills/triage-and-plan.md:1` has no selection metadata and describes repository planning, not ordinary feature implementation. `.swarm/rules/default.md` and lessons must remain inline.
- `internal/workspace/claim_budget_bundle_test.go:74` covers approved planner budget and PR compilation. `internal/workspace/worktree_test.go:15` covers preservation of unmanaged instructions.
- Makefile's `check` runs formatting verification, vet, staticcheck, and one race-enabled full suite.
- The supplied planner SYSTEM_PROMPT.md is 40,154 bytes (`wc -c`). This planning snapshot lacks Git metadata; production compilation and comparable all-role measurements require a normal checkout or a temporary committed fixture.

## What we're assuming

- Optional YAML front matter in skill Markdown is sufficient for selection; no WorkUnit/workflow schema or protected guidance edits are needed. Verify with table-driven parser and selector tests before integrating.
- A 4,096-byte architecture threshold gives a useful deterministic boundary; verify below/at/above the threshold. Keep architecture safety guidance mandatory through project/goals/rules; architecture references are for architectural context.

## Open questions

- The conflicting integration assertion is confirmed: `TestRoleContextAndReviewOnlyLessons` must distinguish WORKUNIT.md from SYSTEM_PROMPT.md as specified in step 4. There is no remaining design question on this behavior; trusted-base tests remain unedited.
- Actual before/after sizes for planner, reviewer, developer, and tester are unknown. Step 1 records the baseline on this repository; step 5 records the updated values with identical inputs. No size claim should be inferred from the supplied planner prompt alone.

## Design and alternatives

Do not infer skill applicability from prose or filenames: those heuristics are hard to explain and unstable. Use optional front matter with `roles: [developer, tester]`, `workflows: [feature]`, and optional `description`. Match role and workflow conjunctively when both are provided; an omitted selector dimension is unrestricted, but a file with neither selector is index-only. An explicit `roles: ["*"]` can request universal inclusion. Reject malformed selectors with an error naming the source file path and offending field rather than silently misselecting guidance. Use the existing YAML dependency and private workspace types, not a new public configuration surface.

List every Markdown skill in sorted path order, with a bounded single-line title/description and approved-source reference. Inline selected bodies once, without YAML metadata; unselected bodies remain outside the prompt. Preserve all rules, project, conventions, goals, SKILLS manual, validation policy, role instructions, and planner budget. Do not move mandatory policy into the optional skill mechanism.

For large architecture documents, write the approved content through safefs to `.swarm/active/ARCHITECTURE.md` and render a bounded section-heading index with a pointer to that snapshot. For skills, provide approved copies under `.swarm/active/guidance/skills/` preserving relative paths, so on-demand reading never directs an agent to candidate skill content. On every compile, rebuild the entire managed `.swarm/active/guidance/` directory from scratch through safefs: remove all old contents and the directory, recreate it, then write only the current approved copies. Use a private recursive helper composed from `Root.OpenDirectory`, `Root.Sub`, and `Root.Remove`; `Root.Remove` alone cannot remove a nonempty directory. Reject symlinks/special files, keep traversal root-bound, and propagate failures before publishing a new prompt. Delete `.swarm/active/ARCHITECTURE.md` through safefs whenever architecture is inlined or absent (missing is harmless). The index must describe these as approved-base copies. Architecture of at most 4,096 bytes remains inline; larger documents use the snapshot. Leave `advance_base.go:staleActiveEvidence` unchanged: its cleanup is followed by authoritative bundle compilation, and unconditional rebuild/removal on every compile handles base changes as well as recompilation without base advancement. Old copies must never survive a successful compile; a cleanup failure aborts compilation before the bundle can be used. Do not read candidate files to build indexes or descriptions.

Order the prompt deterministically: stable repository policy and rules, approved validation policy, role guidance and planner budget, architecture context, skill index and selected bodies, then task-specific feedback and a short instruction to read WORKUNIT.md. Do not include rendered WorkUnit title/objective/constraints/acceptance in the system prompt. Keep workunit.json and artifact evidence behavior intact.

## Exact touchpoints

- `internal/workspace/worktree.go`: CompileHarnessBundleAt and compileHarnessBundle; split rule/skill loading, integrate composition, remove WorkUnit append, preserve safe writes and managed pointers.
- New `internal/workspace/guidance.go`: private approved guidance records, front-matter selection, sorted bounded indexes, architecture threshold, and safe approved-copy helpers.
- `internal/workspace/artifact_context_test.go`: update `TestRoleContextAndReviewOnlyLessons` and its direct `compileHarnessBundle` call. `internal/workspace/filesystem_security_test.go`: mechanically update the direct call in `TestActiveBundleRejectsSymlinkDirectory`; preserve its rejection assertions. Split rule/skill inputs with a private guidance struct parameter on `compileHarnessBundle` and update these two test callers explicitly, along with the production caller.
- New `internal/workspace/guidance_test.go` and `internal/workspace/bundle_guidance_test.go`: pure helper cases and committed-base bundle regression tests, including reproducible role size reporting.
- `changes/unreleased/200-role-guidance-index.md`: concise user-facing behavior change.
- `.swarm/active/IMPLEMENTATION.md`: developer notes, commands/blocked checks, and repository before/after byte-size table for all four roles.
- `.swarm/active/VALIDATION.md`: tester results and acceptance mapping.
- Leave `trusted_config_test.go`, `claim_budget_bundle_test.go`, `pr_test.go`, and `revision_plan_test.go` unedited. No protected harness files, schemas, workflow definitions, or role prompts need modification.

## Implementation sequence

1. Inspect all compilation callers and trusted-base/prompt tests. Before changing behavior, compile all four roles from this repository's approved guidance into disposable scratch copies with identical ISSUE-200 inputs and feature workflow. Record source revision, role, byte counts, and reproduction method in IMPLEMENTATION.md. Do not overwrite active planning artifacts. If checkout history is unavailable, record the blocker and use committed fixtures for tests; obtain real repository measurements when history is available.
2. Add private metadata/index helpers with deterministic selection and bounded summaries; retain every rule inline. Test metadata-less, matching, nonmatching, wildcard, malformed, nested, and empty skills.
3. Integrate approved-base skill copies and architecture snapshots through safefs. Keep enumeration and reads pinned to baseSHA; fail on unreadable enumerated guidance rather than dropping policy. Never fall back to candidate content. Rebuild managed guidance on every compile and delete stale ARCHITECTURE.md when inline/absent, using the root-bound helper above. Add `TestBundleGuidanceBaseTransition`: compile base A with skill X and large architecture, then base B without X and with small architecture into the same destination; assert X copy/index entry and ARCHITECTURE.md are gone. Cover nested deleted/renamed skills, an empty skill set, and repeated compilation. Add adversarial cleanup and threshold tests.
4. Reorder prompt sections, remove embedded WorkUnit, retain explicit read pointers and existing evidence/budget/PR behavior. Update `TestRoleContextAndReviewOnlyLessons`: keep `keep-this-section`, `not current findings`, and role-specific `Superseded previous attempt: …` presence assertions for WORKUNIT.md; for SYSTEM_PROMPT.md require those artifact markers and WorkUnit markers to be absent. Preserve lesson-leak absence assertions in both files and complete REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md assertions. Mechanically update the direct `compileHarnessBundle` calls in artifact_context_test.go and filesystem_security_test.go to the private guidance parameter, preserving symlink rejection. Leave the four named trusted-base test files unedited. Add ordering and unique-task-marker assertions across all four roles and PR wrapper coverage.
5. Add the 20-skill size regression and changelog fragment. Repeat repository role measurements with identical inputs and record before/after bytes in IMPLEMENTATION.md. Run fast changed-package checks and targeted tests; tester records results in VALIDATION.md and runs make check once as the full-suite acceptance run.

No live GitHub flow or external harness execution is required. Related token accounting, skill authoring tools, and automatic semantic skill selection are follow-up work, outside this issue.

## Revision evidence

The two requested revisions are included above: explicit existing-test/caller changes in touchpoints and step 4, and unconditional stale-copy cleanup plus a base A → base B regression in step 3. `internal/workflow/import_policy.go:24` already rejects non-output active-bundle edits in headless imports; no import-policy change is needed. The Claude append-system-prompt-file path depends on the final WORKUNIT.md read pointer, which the ordering test must retain. Planning changes only PLAN.md and TEST_PLAN.md; implementation and validation reports remain assigned to their respective roles.

Developer: notes in IMPLEMENTATION.md, including SYSTEM_PROMPT.md size per role before and after. Tester: results in VALIDATION.md. Run fast checks and targeted tests; at most one full suite.

# Test plan for ISSUE-200

## Acceptance mapping

| Acceptance criterion | Concrete verification |
| --- | --- |
| Safety/policy inline for every role; every skill indexed; only selected skills inline; 20-skill developer size reduction | New `TestBundleGuidanceAllRoles`, `TestSkillSelection`, and `TestBundleTwentySkillsSize`: committed fixture with unique policy markers and 20 sizeable skill bodies; assert rules/project/goals/conventions/manual/validation survive for planner, reviewer, developer, tester. Every skill path appears once in the index; selected body markers appear and all unselected body markers are absent. Compare developer bytes against the legacy composition of the same fixture inputs, not an arbitrary absolute ceiling. Cover role-only, workflow-only, combined AND matching, wildcard, unannotated index-only, malformed metadata with errors naming the source file and field, empty/nested files, deterministic ordering, and bounded summaries. |
| Guidance remains approved-base; candidate skill absent; existing trusted-base tests unchanged | New `TestBundleGuidanceApprovedBase`: commit base guidance, then add a candidate-only skill and modify existing skill metadata/title/body, rules, and architecture. Assert candidate-only name/body and modified markers appear in neither prompt nor approved snapshots; original approved content remains. Include candidate HEAD advancing beyond base, and snapshot symlink rejection. Add `TestBundleGuidanceBaseTransition`: compile base A with skill X and architecture larger than 4,096 bytes, then base B without X and with architecture at most 4,096 bytes into the same destination. Assert X’s approved copy and index entry are absent, ARCHITECTURE.md is deleted, and B’s architecture is inline. Also cover renamed/nested skills, no remaining skills, repeated compilation, and symlink/special-file cleanup rejection without outside writes. Leave `trusted_config_test.go`, `claim_budget_bundle_test.go`, `pr_test.go`, and `revision_plan_test.go` unedited and run them through the workspace package tests. |
| WorkUnit occurs once in WORKUNIT.md; stable policy precedes task text | New `TestBundleWorkUnitAndOrdering`: unique objective/constraint/acceptance markers occur once in WORKUNIT.md and zero times in SYSTEM_PROMPT.md; system prompt points to WORKUNIT.md. Assert stable policy and validation precede role/optional guidance and final task feedback. Compare stable prefix across different task inputs with identical base/role/workflow. Exercise planner CHANGES_REQUESTED and PR wrapper; update existing `TestRoleContextAndReviewOnlyLessons` so WORKUNIT.md retains `keep-this-section`, `not current findings`, and same-role `Superseded previous attempt: …` assertions, while SYSTEM_PROMPT.md asserts those artifact/WorkUnit markers are absent. Keep lesson-leak absence assertions for both files and complete REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md assertions. Mechanically update its direct `compileHarnessBundle` call and the one in `TestActiveBundleRejectsSymlinkDirectory` for the private guidance parameter; keep symlink rejection and unmanaged instruction tests intact. |
| make check passes | Fast changed-package checks first, then one `make check` run covering formatting, repository vet/staticcheck, and the race-enabled full suite. Record outcome in VALIDATION.md; report environment blockers honestly. |

Additional objective coverage: `TestArchitectureGuidanceThreshold` checks below/at/above 4,096 bytes, section-index bounds, small-document inline behavior, full approved snapshot content, and candidate architecture exclusion. Empty/default role and nil/empty workflow handling must preserve supported caller behavior without panics.

## Commands and execution budget

For the proposed source changes, run:

```bash
gofmt -l internal/workspace/worktree.go internal/workspace/guidance.go internal/workspace/guidance_test.go internal/workspace/bundle_guidance_test.go internal/workspace/artifact_context_test.go internal/workspace/filesystem_security_test.go
go vet ./internal/workspace
go tool staticcheck ./internal/workspace
go test ./internal/workspace -run 'Test(SkillSelection|ArchitectureGuidanceThreshold|BundleGuidance|RoleContextAndReviewOnlyLessons|ActiveBundleRejectsSymlinkDirectory|BundleTwentySkillsSize|BundleWorkUnitAndOrdering|PlannerBundle|HarnessCleanup|CompilePRHarnessBundle)' -count=1
go test ./internal/workspace
make check
```

Format changed Go files before the read-only formatting check. If integration requires other packages, include those packages in the fast checks and targeted tests. Targeted package runs are allowed; run at most one full repository suite, through `make check`. Do not separately run `go test ./...` or `make race`. Build-only approved checks may use `go build ./...` without consuming the full-suite allowance. Use writable scratch Go cache/temp directories if needed; no credential requests or coordinator validation commands.

## Repository prompt-size evidence

Developer records an IMPLEMENTATION.md table with planner/reviewer/developer/tester rows, before bytes, after bytes, delta, repository approved-source revision, and reproducible compilation inputs. Use byte lengths of generated SYSTEM_PROMPT.md with the same WorkUnit, feature workflow, and empty artifact list before and after; generate into scratch destinations. Preserve this repository's approved guidance rather than substituting the 20-skill fixture. The supplied active planner file measures 40,154 bytes, but is contextual evidence only because invocation inputs may differ. Tester verifies the table and records results in VALIDATION.md. Missing Git history in a snapshot is a recorded measurement limitation, never a fabricated measurement.

The 20-skill fixture is the automated size assertion required by acceptance; repository measurements explain the actual effect here and need not show the same percentage reduction.

## Reporting

Developer notes and developer check output belong in `.swarm/active/IMPLEMENTATION.md`. Tester acceptance results, exact commands, failures, and blocked checks belong in `.swarm/active/VALIDATION.md`. This planning phase changes Markdown artifacts only and does not run source checks or consume the full-suite budget.

## Managed-copy lifecycle

Every compile removes and recreates guidance/ through root-bound safefs operations, including nonempty nested directories, and removes ARCHITECTURE.md for inline or absent architecture. Tests must exercise successful cleanup and fail-closed cleanup errors before prompt publication. This unconditional rebuild makes adding paths to staleActiveEvidence unnecessary; the base-transition regression verifies the same destination cannot retain A guidance after successful compilation at B. No recursive host-path deletion is permitted.

VERDICT: APPROVED

# Review of ISSUE-200 plan (revision 2)

Both revisions requested earlier have been made. The plan covers every acceptance criterion and the changelog constraint, and it stays within scope. Its evidence citations match the code in this snapshot.

## Audit

| Item | Plan / test plan coverage | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Objective: universal policy/safety inline | Rules, project, conventions, goals, SKILLS manual, validation policy, role prompt and budget stay inline; mandatory policy is kept out of the optional mechanism | ✅ |
| Objective: skill index + role/workflow selection | Front matter `roles`/`workflows`/`description`; AND matching; wildcard; unannotated files are index-only; malformed selectors fail and name the file and field | ✅ |
| Objective: reference large architecture | Above 4,096 bytes: approved snapshot `.swarm/active/ARCHITECTURE.md` plus a heading index; tested below, at and above the threshold | ✅ |
| Objective: remove duplicated WorkUnit; stable text first | Drops the `workunitMD` append (worktree.go:909–910); fixed section order ending with a pointer to WORKUNIT.md; prefix-stability test | ✅ |
| AC1: 20-skill developer size drop, every skill named | `TestBundleTwentySkillsSize`, compared against the legacy composition of the same inputs; `TestBundleGuidanceAllRoles` | ✅ |
| AC2: approved base only; no candidate skill; trusted-base tests unchanged | `TestBundleGuidanceApprovedBase` (candidate-only and modified skill, rules, architecture); four named test files left unedited | ✅ |
| AC3: WorkUnit once; ordering | `TestBundleWorkUnitAndOrdering` across four roles and the PR wrapper; updated `TestRoleContextAndReviewOnlyLessons` | ✅ |
| AC4: make check | Run once by the tester; recorded in VALIDATION.md | ✅ |
| Constraint: changelog fragment | `changes/unreleased/200-role-guidance-index.md` | ✅ |
| Shape fit (Involved) | Alternatives rejected with reasons (prose/filename inference); assumptions labelled, with verification steps | ✅ |
| Protected paths | No edits to harness, prompts, rules or skills; allow_harness_changes=false respected | ✅ |
| Operator guidance | The test and both call sites are named; guidance/ is rebuilt on every compile; ARCHITECTURE.md is deleted when inline or absent; base A→B test; size table per role; one full suite | ✅ |

## Evidence verified

- `worktree.go:774` CompileHarnessBundleAt, `:804–822` inline all rules/skills, `:871–874` WORKUNIT.md write, `:909–910` WorkUnit appended to the prompt: confirmed.
- `pr.go:21` delegates to CompileHarnessBundleAt: confirmed.
- Direct `compileHarnessBundle` callers are only `artifact_context_test.go:23` and `filesystem_security_test.go:23`, both named in the plan.
- The current `TestRoleContextAndReviewOnlyLessons` asserts `keep-this-section` / `Superseded previous attempt` in **both** files. The plan's split (present in WORKUNIT.md, absent from SYSTEM_PROMPT.md) is the change this requires.
- None of the four "leave unedited" tests assert WorkUnit text or section order in SYSTEM_PROMPT.md: `claim_budget_bundle_test.go` checks the budget text, `pr_test.go` checks `## PR revision`, `revision_plan_test.go` writes its own prompt, and `trusted_config_test.go` does not read the prompt. Keeping them unedited is feasible.
- `safefs.Root` has `OpenDirectory`, `Sub` and `Remove` (root.go:92/136/254) and no recursive remove, so the private helper is justified.
- `import_policy.go:24` rejects non-output `.swarm/active/**` edits, so the new guidance/ and ARCHITECTURE.md files are covered. `.swarm/active/` is gitignored.
- Claude/omp adapters (`adapters.go:111–119`) pass only the system prompt file and task prompt. The final pointer to WORKUNIT.md in SYSTEM_PROMPT.md therefore matters, and the plan keeps it and tests for it.
- Review and worker snapshots (`agent/review.go:149`, `sandbox/worker.go:642`) walk nested directories generically. A nested guidance/ tree is compatible and bounded by skill count.
- The snapshot has no `.git`, which confirms the stated measurement limitation. The 40,154-byte planner figure cannot be checked here (the active reviewer prompt is 36,950 bytes), but the test plan correctly treats it only as context.

## Non-blocking notes for the developer

1. **Absent directories vs unreadable files.** Today a missing `.swarm/rules` or `.swarm/skills` is tolerated (an `ls-tree` error is skipped). The plan's "fail on unreadable enumerated guidance" should apply only to files that were enumerated. A base with no skills or rules directory must still compile; the "no remaining skills" case should cover this.
2. **Repository skill becomes index-only.** `.swarm/skills/triage-and-plan.md` has no front matter. After this change it is index-only for every role, with its approved copy under `.swarm/active/guidance/skills/`. That is intended. Adding front matter would be a protected-path edit and belongs in a follow-up WorkUnit with `allow_harness_changes: true`.
3. **Formatting command.** Use `gofmt -s -l` in the fast check to match the approved `fmt` policy and the Makefile `lint` target.
4. **Fail-closed order.** Do guidance/ cleanup and ARCHITECTURE.md removal before writing SYSTEM_PROMPT.md, so a cleanup failure never leaves a new prompt pointing at stale copies.

## Follow-ups (out of scope)

- Add selection front matter to the repository's own skills (needs harness-change authorization).
- Token accounting and skill authoring tooling, as the plan already notes.

# Implementation notes for ISSUE-200

## Summary

I implemented the approved plan. Role prompts now include all mandatory policy inline. Skills appear in an index, and a skill's body is inlined only when its front matter selects the current role and workflow. Large architecture documents are referenced by section instead of inlined. The WorkUnit text now lives only in WORKUNIT.md, and stable policy comes before task-specific text.

## Changes

- **`internal/workspace/guidance.go` (new)**: private helpers, no exported surface.
  - `parseGuidanceSkill` reads optional YAML front matter (`roles`, `workflows`, `description`). Malformed metadata (scalar or empty lists, non-string or blank items, names containing spaces, an unclosed block, invalid YAML) returns an error that names the skill path and the field.
  - Selection: every selector that is present must match, `"*"` matches any role, and a skill with no selectors is index-only.
  - `renderSkillGuidance` lists every skill in path order on one line each, with titles and descriptions capped at 160 runes. Each entry either says "inlined below" or gives the path of the approved copy. Selected bodies are inlined once, with front matter stripped.
  - `renderArchitecture`: documents up to 4,096 bytes (after trimming) are inlined. Larger ones get a section index (at most 40 headings, with fenced code skipped) and a pointer to `.swarm/active/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
  - `writeApprovedGuidance` and `removeManagedTree` handle the managed copies. On every compile, `.swarm/active/guidance/` is removed and rebuilt. The helper is built from `safefs.Root.OpenDirectory` and `Remove`, uses batched `ReadDir(128)`, and is depth-bounded. It refuses symlinks and special files. `ARCHITECTURE.md` is written only when the architecture is referenced rather than inlined, and is deleted otherwise (a missing file is fine).
- **`internal/workspace/worktree.go`**:
  - `CompileHarnessBundleAt` now splits approved guidance into `bundleGuidance{policy, skills}`. Policy is goals, SKILLS.md and every rule. Rules and skills are listed from the approved base with `ls-tree -r -z --name-only <base> -- <dir>` via the new `approvedMarkdownFiles`. A file that was listed but can't be read, or a malformed skill, now fails compilation. A directory missing from the base still lists nothing, as reviewer note 1 asked. Nothing is read from the candidate tree.
  - `compileHarnessBundle` now takes `bundleGuidance` instead of `extraDocs ...string`. It rebuilds the approved copies *before* writing workunit.json, WORKUNIT.md or SYSTEM_PROMPT.md, so a failed cleanup never publishes a new prompt (reviewer note 4).
  - Prompt order is now: project, conventions, goals, SKILLS manual, rules, validation policy, role prompt, planner claim budget, architecture, skill index and selected skills, planner CHANGES_REQUESTED note, `---`, then a short `# Task` pointer to `.swarm/active/WORKUNIT.md`. The rendered WorkUnit is no longer appended. For PRs, `## PR revision` is still appended after the pointer by `WriteRevisionContext`, which is unchanged.
- **Test callers updated as the plan named them**:
  - `artifact_context_test.go`: `TestRoleContextAndReviewOnlyLessons` now requires `keep-this-section`, `not current findings`, same-role `Superseded previous attempt: …` and new WorkUnit title/objective markers to be present in WORKUNIT.md and absent from SYSTEM_PROMPT.md. It also requires SYSTEM_PROMPT.md to point to WORKUNIT.md. The lesson-leak and REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md assertions are unchanged.
  - `filesystem_security_test.go`: `TestActiveBundleRejectsSymlinkDirectory` got the mechanical parameter change only.
- **New tests**:
  - `guidance_test.go`: `TestSkillSelection`, `TestSkillSelectionRejectsMalformedMetadata`, `TestSkillTitlesAndIndex`, `TestArchitectureGuidanceThreshold` (empty, 4095, 4096 and 4097 bytes; fences; heading cap), and `TestRemoveManagedTree` (nested, missing, and refused symlinks with nothing outside touched).
  - `bundle_guidance_test.go`, against committed-base fixtures:
    - `TestBundleGuidanceAllRoles`
    - `TestBundleTwentySkillsSize`
    - `TestBundleGuidanceApprovedBase` (candidate changes uncommitted, and committed beyond base)
    - `TestBundleGuidanceBaseTransition` (base A, then B, then C: deleted, renamed and nested skills, repeated compilation, and a base with no skills or rules)
    - `TestBundleGuidanceCleanupFailsClosed`
    - `TestBundleWorkUnitAndOrdering` (all four roles × issue and PR wrapper, planner CHANGES_REQUESTED, stable prefix)
- **`changes/unreleased/200-role-guidance-index.md`**: changelog fragment.
- Unedited, as planned: `trusted_config_test.go`, `claim_budget_bundle_test.go`, `pr_test.go`, `revision_plan_test.go`, `advance_base.go`, and every protected path.

Mutation check: with the `removeManagedTree` call disabled, `TestBundleGuidanceBaseTransition` fails with "base A guidance survived compilation at base B". Restored afterwards.

## SYSTEM_PROMPT.md size per role (this repository)

**Method.** I used a temporary env-gated test, `internal/workspace/zz_measure_tmp_test.go`, which I deleted after measuring. It copies this snapshot's `.swarm/` (excluding `.swarm/active`), `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` into a scratch Git repo and commits them as the base. It then runs `CompileHarnessBundleAt` once per role with:

- the WorkUnit from `.swarm/active/workunit.json` (ISSUE-200),
- the `feature` workflow loaded from that base,
- an empty artifact list.

The "before" run used the unmodified source; the "after" run used the final source.

**Limitation.** The snapshot has no Git metadata, so the approved source revision is "this task snapshot's `.swarm/` tree" rather than a SHA. Allow Harness Changes is false, so this tree is the approved guidance.

| Role | Before (bytes) | After (bytes) | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| planner | 19,802 | 13,357 | −6,445 (−32.5%) |
| reviewer | 18,032 | 11,587 | −6,445 (−35.7%) |
| developer | 19,659 | 13,214 | −6,445 (−32.8%) |
| tester | 17,588 | 11,143 | −6,445 (−36.6%) |

The delta is identical for every role. Two things remove text: `triage-and-plan.md` (no front matter) is now index-only, and the WorkUnit text is no longer duplicated. The skill index adds back a few hundred bytes. The 20-skill fixture in `TestBundleTwentySkillsSize` logs 11,262 bytes for the developer prompt with the index, against 49,312 bytes if every skill were inlined.

## Checks run

Approved required checks, run directly from the snapshot root (`GOCACHE` pointed at a scratch dir):

# Validation report for ISSUE-200 (tester, provisional)

**Verdict: PASS with one environmental exception.** All acceptance criteria are verified by tests that pass. `make check` could not run as a single command here, because the tool limits each shell call to 2 minutes. I ran its two parts instead: `make lint`, then one race-enabled full suite split into package and test shards. Every package passes except `internal/agent`, where one sandbox test fails. The cause is a missing `/root` directory on this host, which is unrelated to this change (details below).

The coordinator replaces this file with its authoritative report.

## Commands and results

`GOCACHE` defaults to `$HOME/.cache/go-build`. `/tmp` and `$HOME` do not persist between tool calls here, so each shard rebuilt from scratch.

| --- | --- | --- |
| fmt (approved) | `gofmt -s -l .` | clean, no output |
| build (approved) | `go build ./...` | ok |

### Race suite shards (this is the single full-suite run)

- `go test -race` for `cmd/swarm`, `internal/{changelog,contract,coordination,fork,gitcredential,harness}`: ok. This was the first shard; it reached the 115 s timeout after these packages had reported, so I re-ran the remaining packages in smaller groups.
- `internal/{lease,node,pr,process,progress,registry}`: ok
- `internal/{safefs,sandbox,tracker,validation,workflow}`: ok
- `internal/workspace`: ok (25.4 s)
- `internal/cli`: built once with `go test -race -c`. I ran 4 `-test.run` shards: `^Test[ABDEFGHJLM]` (35 tests), `^Test[INPRSUVW]` (95), `^(TestC[a-z]|TestCLI[A-O])` (54), `^TestCLI[P-Z]` (52). That is 236 of 236 tests, and every shard printed PASS. I checked shard membership with `-test.list`. One earlier shard regex (`^TestC[A-K]`) matched no tests, so I discarded it and did not count it.
- `internal/agent`: **FAIL**, `TestReviewerSandboxAllowsScratchButDeniesSourceAndCredentials` (`review_test.go:201: reviewer agent failed (exit 1; harness diagnostics withheld)`). Every other test in the package passes.

### `internal/agent` failure: root cause (environmental)

Running the test under `strace` showed the redacted 48-byte diagnostic: `bwrap: Can't mkdir /root: Read-only file system`. `internal/sandbox/sandbox.go:167` wraps the reviewer with `--ro-bind / / ... --tmpfs /root`, and this host has no `/root` (`ls -ld /root` → No such file or directory) with a read-only `/`. Bubblewrap itself works here: the test's `/bin/true` probe exits 0. The test only skips on `Operation not permitted`, so this failure is reported instead of skipped.

This is unrelated to ISSUE-200. The change does not touch `internal/sandbox` or `internal/agent`, and the test never compiles a bundle. The developer's suspicion was correct; this confirms the cause. Possible follow-up outside this WorkUnit: either have the read-only wrapper tolerate hosts without `/root`, or widen the test's skip to cover this case.
